title.en: The Ghost and the Invention Device

summary.en: The exhibition tells a story about the Ghost of the Museum.

ai.en: An interactive exhibition for children aged 5 to 9 at the Museum of Technology, where they learn about inventions through play and tasks, then switch on the Ghost's Invention Device.

events.description: The exhibition tells a story about the Ghost of the Museum. The Ghost requests children to learn about technology via play, mysteries, hands-on tasks and inventing. The exhibition includes different areas with different viewpoints into technology: essence of technology, stages of invention, values and relevance of technology, collaboration, Finnish inventions and changes that have taken place in technology in the long run. As a culmination of the museum tour children can switch on The Ghost’s Invention Device by using the new skills they have learned in the exhibition. The Ghost and the Invention Device is an interactive and child-centered learning environment that includes versatile learning methods. The environment together with museum objects support children’s creative museum engagement and encourages them to observe, handle and understand technology as a part of their everyday life. summary.en: The heart of the Sinebrychoff Art Museum is the unique home of Paul and Fanny Sinebrychoff, which has been on permanent display

ai.en: The Sinebrychoff family's historic town house, on permanent display at the Sinebrychoff Art Museum. Entry is free.

events.description: The heart of the Sinebrychoff Art Museum is the unique home of Paul and Fanny Sinebrychoff, which has been on permanent display on the second floor of the building since 27 November 1921. The Sinebrychoffs’ palatial town house at Bulevardi 40 was completed in 1842. The building was immediately considered to be one of the most significant private homes in Helsinki. The last occupants of the house bearing the name Sinebrychoff, Paul and Fanny Sinebrychoff, were passionate art enthusiasts. They collected the most beautiful European art and objects for their home. When their collections were donated to the Finnish state in 1921, they comprised more than 900 items. Paul and Fanny’s wish to open the doors of their home to the public to see the art treasures they had collected was recorded in a will almost one hundred years ago. The same spirit still lives on in the museum. Sinebrychoff Art Museum 27.11.2021-31.1.2040 Free entry

title.en: Tove Jansson Gallery: Artist Family Jansson

summary.en: The Tove Jansson Gallery at HAM opens on a larger scale than ever before, now spreading across three exhibition halls.

ai.en: The Tove Jansson Gallery at HAM, across three halls, with its first show on the Jansson family of artists. It marks 80 years of "Comet in Moominland".

events.description: The Tove Jansson Gallery at HAM opens on a larger scale than ever before, now spreading across three exhibition halls. The Tove Jansson Gallery is built around the beloved frescos Party in the Countryside and Party in the City, which are permanently on display. Spanning three exhibition halls, the gallery aims to strengthen Tove Jansson’s artistic legacy and significance in both art history and Finnish society. It showcases Jansson’s art in a diverse way and introduces new perspectives on her as both a Helsinki-based and international artist. The gallery’s first exhibition presents the diverse forms of expression and shared artistic projects of the Jansson family of artists. Photographs also provide a glimpse into the family’s leisure time. The home’s atmosphere, close relationships and shared family adventures were later reflected in the Moomin stories that launched Tove Jansson to international fame. The Artist Family Jansson exhibition commemorates the book Comet in Moominland, which is celebrating its 80th anniversary in 2026. Helsinki Art Museum HAM 13.2.2026-10.1.2027 Admission fee 0-20€

events.description: The exhibition unfolds like a dream: fragmentary and wondrous, interweaving fantasy and reality. Visitors encounter a space where the possible and impossible hover side by side, evoking experiences that words cannot fully capture. The exhibition presents works from the Finnish National Gallery’s collection, which holds over 43,000 works in total. It features around 40 artists, including Eija-Liisa Ahtila, Riikka Anttonen, Milla Aska, Korakrit Arunanondchai, Bruce Nauman, Olli Lyytikäinen, Elina Merenmies, Pakui Hardware, and Cindy Sherman.

title.en: Anna Sinebrychoff - Ahead of Her Time

summary.en: Anna Sinebrychoff (1830–1904) had a bourgeois girl’s education, married the successful businessman Paul Sinebrychoff (1799–1883) in 1850.

ai.en: A display on Anna Sinebrychoff, a 19th-century Helsinki businesswoman who led her family's brewery and was known for her charity work.

events.description: Anna Sinebrychoff (1830–1904) had a bourgeois girl’s education, married the successful businessman Paul Sinebrychoff (1799–1883) in 1850, and they had four children. On her husband’s death, she attained a position that was rare for a woman in Finland, as majority shareholder and chair of the board of a large company. In the latter half of the 19th century, she became the most important woman in the prominent Sinebrychoff Brewery clan. She resolutely led the family and kept a close eye on the work of her two sons as they managed the company. She was the undisputed matriarch and a revered grandmother. Anna Sinebrychoff died in 1904. The numerous obituaries noted her extensive charitable work. The exhibition offers a broad overview of Anna’s life and work in Helsinki from the 1850s onwards. At its core is Anna Sinebrychoff the active influencer: bearer of responsibility for the family and business, benefactor, prominent figure in associations and societies, and member of the Orthodox congregation. Sinebrychoff Art Museum, Red Cellar 3.3.2026-29.8.2027 Tue, Thu, Fri 11.00-18.00 Wed 10.00-20.00 Sat-Sun 10.00-17.00 Admission fee 0-21€

events.description: The touring exhibition organized by the Finnish Glass Museum celebrates the inclusion of handmade glassmaking on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. The exhibition presents the tradition of handmade glass and highlights Finnish glassmaking activities and expertise. Glass has been blown in Suomenlinna since the 1970s. The studio glass activity initiated by Heikki Kallio has been continued by Glass Studio Hytti, which has hosted several makers of both functional and art glass. The touring exhibition has been complemented with works by Heikki Kallio and glass artists who have worked in Suomenlinna in the 2020s. title.en: Paper Stars – Paper Dolls by Rauni Palonen

summary.en: Paper Stars – Paper Dolls by Rauni Palonen, 1968–1982

ai.en: A small exhibition at Tamminiemi of paper dolls by Rauni Palonen, drawn for Apu magazine from 1968 to 1982, showing celebrities of the Kekkonen era.

events.description: Paper Stars – Paper Dolls by Rauni Palonen, 1968–1982 Tamminiemi features a nostalgic glimpse into the world of celebrities and popular culture of President Kekkonen’s era. The small-scale exhibition showcases paper dolls drawn by fashion artist and editor Rauni Palonen (b. 1929). Originally published in Apu magazine between 1968 and 1982, these drawings depicted the most celebrated stars of the era: beauty queens, singers, actors, television personalities, athletes, and even royalty from neighbouring countries. Palonen would produce weekly sketches of celebrities, complete with outfits tailored to the latest fashion trends. For many, these paper stars were treasured toys. They were carefully cut out, glued to cardboard, accessorised with handmade outfits, and preserved with care. Several of these paper stars were also a familiar sight at Kekkonen’s home in Tamminiemi or at the Independence Day reception at the Presidential Palace. Paper Stars is a tribute to the long and distinguished career of fashion editor Rauni Palonen, whose paper dolls were known to the entire nation in her time. The collection donated by Palonen to the Finnish Heritage Agency’s Picture Collections contains a total of 207 paper stars. In this small-scale exhibition, approximately 80 figures are on display, featuring both digitised versions and original drawings. Tamminiemi 17.4.2026-9.1.2028

events.description: The world of pollinators comes to life! How does a bee perceive the world? What would disappear from our dining table without pollinators? And did you know that mosquitoes, wasps, and even snails also pollinate flowers? The exhibition offers fascinating information about pollinators, stunning visuals, and engaging activities. Visitors can play the interactive "Identify the Pollinators" game and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the Natural History Museum's remarkable specimens. summary.en: Solve the mystery of Plague Park through five location-based puzzles and follow the shadows of the past in the heart of Helsinki.

ai.en: A location-based puzzle game in the Old Church Park, known as Plague Park, from 22 May to 31 October 2026. It is free and uses five puzzles across the park.

events.description: Solve the mystery of Plague Park through five location-based puzzles and follow the shadows of the past in the heart of Helsinki. By the edge of Bulevardi lies a park where thousands of Helsinkians from centuries past rest beneath the ground. Today it is a sunny green space, but in 1710 it was the final resting place for victims of the plague. Now known as the Old Church Park, it is perhaps better known by its nickname: Plague Park. Can you follow the shadows of the past and solve the secret buried deep within the park? The game's narrator, Mrs. Granstedt, has seen ghosts in the park since she was a child. Follow her tracks and a mysterious little creature through five location-based puzzles all around the park. Open the game: ruttopuisto.epicscape.game Old Church Park - Plague Park 22.5.-31.10.2026 Free of charge

summary.en: The exhibition invites visitors to explore Alvar,  Aino and Elissa Aalto’s architecture and design from the perspective of wellbeing.

ai.en: An exhibition on the Aaltos' architecture and design through the lens of wellbeing, with drawings, furniture and a calm Aalto Lounge.

events.description: The exhibition invites visitors to explore Alvar, Aino and Elissa Aalto’s architecture and design from the perspective of wellbeing. The exhibition highlights wellbeing as the Aaltos’ major contribution to Western architectural modernism and examines how their work and philosophy approach it as a balance between people, nature, the built environment, and materials. It connects the Aaltos’ idea of holistic wellbeing with contemporary thinking and the growing desire to understand wellbeing as extending beyond the individual to concern the whole planet. The exhibition brings together a diverse dialogue of presentation methods and materials, including drawings and scale models, furniture, glass objects and material experiments, as well as artworks. The exhibition also features rarely displayed items from the museum’s collections. Among other works, the exhibition includes the multi-channel video installation Other Actors (2025) by London-based artist and researcher Ilona Sagar. The Aalto Lounge offers a calm space for rest and reflection and invites visitors to explore how being in a space affects their body and mind in the presence of authentic Aalto objects. Architecture and Design Museum 5.6.2026-6.1.2027 Admission fee 0-23€ Further information about the exhibition and public program will be announced at a later date.

Tarinoita pelon ja toivon vuosikymmeniltä:
Esa Leskisen Toinen tasavalta kertoo Suomen ponnisteluista säilyttää demokraattinen valtiomuotonsa.

ai.en: "Toinen tasavalta" at the National Theatre's Main Stage, a 2026 play on Finland's postwar years, with Urho Kekkonen at its centre. It is in Finnish and runs 2 hours 45 minutes.

events.description: Tarinoita pelon ja toivon vuosikymmeniltä Esa Leskisen Toinen tasavalta kertoo Suomen ponnisteluista säilyttää demokraattinen valtiomuotonsa Neuvostoliiton painostuksen, kansainvälisten konfliktien ja sisäisten poliittisten ristiriitojen puristuksessa. Esitys on Leskisen demokratia-aiheisen esityssarjan itsenäinen neljäs osa, jonka edeltäjä oli huippusuosittu Ensimmäinen tasavalta (2022). Toinen tasavalta on älykäs, viihdyttävä ja elävän ajankuvan värittämä esitys, joka vyöryttää kansalliselle päänäyttämölle historian äkkikäänteitä ja henkilöitä sodanjälkeisistä vaaran vuosista 1980-luvun juppiaikaan ja neuvostoimperiumin romahdukseen. events.description: The Modern Classics series of exhibitions presents 20th-century artists from the Finnish National Gallery collections. The first artist to be featured in the series is Elga Sesemann. Elga Sesemann’s (1922–2007) life story is an exceptional and interesting example of a professional woman artist making a career for herself in Finland. The artist’s very first solo exhibition in Helsinki, in 1945, already drew the attention of critics and the art audience to her expressive style. Sesemann’s artistic oeuvre is extensive, and she enjoyed an active career, with her expression constantly evolving, until the mid-1990s. Ateneum Art Museum 18.8.2026-8.8.2027

title.en: Daniel Kruger: Fragments of the Future

summary.en: A Three-Generation Dialogue: From Tools to Artworks – Antti Favén, Mauri Favén, and Aino Favén.

ai.en: A first solo show in Helsinki by South African-born artist Daniel Kruger, with jewellery and ceramics that mix nature, history and everyday objects. Entry is free.

events.description: The first solo exhibition in Helsinki by internationally acclaimed South African-born artist Daniel Kruger (b. 1951) presents his distinctive jewellery and ceramic works. Kruger’s art brings together influences from his upbringing in South Africa and Namibia with decades of working in Germany – creating a dialogue between nature and culture, history and the present, and the precious and the everyday. Kruger is known for his fearless combinations of materials and techniques. Precious metals, gemstones and pearls may appear alongside glass, paper, textiles, pigments and found objects. His sculptural jewellery is at once made to adorn the body, to be touched and handled, and to exist as an autonomous work of art. In his ceramics, history, ornament and contemporary culture often take on unexpected and playful forms. Fragments of the Future explores memory, material and the layers of time. For Kruger, the past is not a closed archive but a living reservoir from which objects, forms and memories can enter new contexts and move towards the future. The exhibition invites us to look at familiar materials and objects from a new perspective – with sensuality, curiosity and an open mind. Gallery GAo ShAn 21.8.-24.10.2026 Tue-Fri 12.00-18.00 Sat 12.00-16.00 Free entry

summary.en: The concert is a synthesis of luohti, electronic music, jouhikko and video art that explores the contemporary expression of the Sámi worldview.

ai.en: An audiovisual concert at Kiasma Theatre, combining Sámi yoiks by Ánnámáret with electronic music and video. The ticket includes Kiasma's exhibitions that day.

events.description: Bálvvosbáiki is an audiovisual concert in which the Sámi yoiks (luohtis) performed by Ánnámáret intertwine with Turkka Inkilä’s nuanced electronic music, Ilkka Heinonen’s gritty and partially effected jouhikko, and Marja Viitahuhta’s video art combining animation, archival footage, and material filmed in Sápmi. The luohtis reflect how the Sámi worldview manifests in the present day, while the concert also touches on themes of colonialism and environmental awareness. Are the female deities Sáráhkka, Juhksáhkka and Uksáhkka still present? Can the power of a sieidi be experienced through yoiking? What does intergenerational sorrow feel like? The concert is part of Kiasma's We Who Remain - Sámi Art in Focus exhibition's programme. Ticket includes admission to Kiasma's exhibitions on the day of the performance.

ai.en: "Orvot", a new Finnish-language play at the National Theatre's Taivassali, about two orphaned brothers whose lives change when a stranger arrives. Premieres 2 September 2026.

events.description: Tarina vapaudesta, veljeydestä ja väkivallasta Veljekset Treat ja Phillip ovat orpoja. Heidän ailahteleva isänsä on häipynyt ja äiti kuollut poikien ollessa pieniä. Koko tähänastisen elämänsä nuoret miehet ovat asuneet kahdestaan rivitalomurjussa Pohjois-Philadelphiassa. Lapsenkaltainen Phillip (Juho Uusitalo) ei koskaan poistu asunnosta, koska hän potee hengenvaarallista allergiaa. Tai niin ainakin hänen isoveljensä Treat (Pyry Nikkilä) väittää. Elämä ikkunan takana on Phillipille kiehtovaa, pelottavaa ‒ ja ehdottomasti kiellettyä. Epävakaa ja väkivaltainen Treat hankkii heille elannon rikoksilla. Eräänä iltana Treat tuo asunnolle humalaisen Haroldin (Petri Liski), jolla on mukanaan kallisarvoinen osakesalkku. Myös Harold on orpo, joka on viettänyt lapsuutensa laitoksessa. Treat ottaa Haroldin panttivangiksi aikomuksenaan vaatia miljoonalunnaat tämän ystäviltä. Pian paljastuu, ettei Harold olekaan ihan tavallinen kaduntallaaja, eivätkä sitä ole myöskään Haroldin oletetut ystävät. Harold tekee veljeksille yllättävän tarjouksen, joka mullistaa heidän elämänsä. Mutta voiko rikkinäinen sielu päästä karkuun menneisyyttä, saati omaa itseään? summary.en: Creative Destruction – A photographic series by Johan Eichhorn

ai.en: Johan Eichhorn's staged photographs move forest roads and drained wetlands into domestic spaces, asking why we accept such changes in nature. At the Natural History Museum until January 2027.

events.description: Johan Eichhorn’s Creative Destruction shifts human interventions in nature into the human living environment. Instead of forest roads cutting through woodlands, drainage drying out wetlands, and dams altering waterways, these elements appear in people’s homes and other everyday spaces. In the staged photographs, familiar environments become strange. At the same time, they make visible the ways we reshape nature – changes that have gradually become an almost unnoticed part of our daily lives. The exhibition does not aim to provide answers, but invites viewers to reflect on why we accept in nature things we would never accept in our own living environment. Natural History Museum 1.9.2026-10.1.2027

title.en: Caring for & Commoning the Urban Dark

summary.en: Darkness Library Suomenlinna is a wooden pavilion that gathers and shares residents’ site-specific knowledge of darkness in Suomenlinna.

ai.en: A wooden pavilion called Darkness Library Suomenlinna at Levyhalli, which gathers local knowledge about darkness. It is free and runs until 25 October 2026.

events.description: Darkness Library Suomenlinna is a wooden pavilion that gathers and shares residents’ site-specific knowledge of darkness in Suomenlinna. Developed within the Caring Commons research project, it explores how creative practices can strengthen human–nature relationships and contribute to sustainability transformation. It asks: How could a darker Helsinki support the well-being of people, wildlife, and nature? Can darkness be described as site-specific? How do darkness and environment support one another? What emerges in a place because of its darkness? The research is funded by the Nessling Foundation and conducted by postdoctoral researcher Gloria Lauterbach, NODUS Sustainable Design Research Group at Aalto University. The wooden pavilion is built in collaboration with the Department of Architecture, Aalto University. Levyhalli 1.9.–25.10.2026 1.–6.9. Daily 13.00–18.00 7.–30.9. summary.en: Isabella Chydenius: Depictions of nightly (club) corners

ai.en: Sculptures by Isabella Chydenius on safer-space club culture and queer nightlife, shown at MUU Window from 10 September to 1 November 2026. Free and open 24/7.

events.description: Isabella Chydenius: Depictions of nightly (club) corners The sculptures in this exhibition highlight elements of Chydenius research into safer space club culture and queer nightlife. The rigid square shapes reference heteropatriarchal norms that seek to control and contain people who challenge said norms, while simultaneously suggesting the outlines of a protected space for safety, community, and self-expression. The light inside the sculptures acts as a metaphor for the joy and empowerment created within nightclubs. As the light escapes the square’s boundaries, it symbolically challenges the limits imposed by oppressive structures. MUU Ikkuna 10.9.-1.11.2026 24/7 Free entry

Myöhemmin myös näitä piirustuksia hyödyntäen etsittiin erilaisista kangas vaihtoehdoista sopivia värejä ja kankaita mandalaan. Lidia jatkoi kuviosabluunoiden tekoa suunnitellun kuvion mukaan. summary.en: This exhibition delves into the bold and multifaceted world of the beloved artist Elin Danielson-Gambogi (1861–1919).

ai.en: An exhibition on painter Elin Danielson-Gambogi's self-portraits and her identity as a woman and artist, at the Didrichsen Art Museum until January 2027.

events.description: This exhibition delves into the bold and multifaceted world of the beloved artist Elin Danielson-Gambogi (1861–1919). Her works reveal the artist’s exploration of the roles of woman, artist, and individual at the crossroads of two cultures, and how she built her identity through art at a time when women were not yet allowed that right. Danielson’s self-portraits, intimate depictions of everyday life, and the tensions within her gazes tell a story of self-discovery and the defense of one’s own voice – themes that continue to resonate today. Didrichsen Art Museum 12.9.2026–31.1.2027 Tue-Sun 11.00-18.00

summary.en: Katariina Nummisen ja Milja Sarkolan tulkinta Nobel-palkitun Imre Kertészin romaanista on kiehtova ja puhutteleva näyttämöpalapeli historiasta.

ai.en: "Lopetus", a stage version of Imre Kertész's Nobel-winning novel, following a publisher's search for a lost manuscript. It is at the National Theatre's Small Stage from 15 September to 19 December 2026.

events.description: Katariina Nummisen ja Milja Sarkolan tulkinta Nobel-palkitun Imre Kertészin romaanista on kiehtova ja puhutteleva näyttämöpalapeli historiasta, muistista ja menneisyyden pitkästä varjosta. Kirjailija B on tehnyt itsemurhan. Arvoituksellisen B:n jälkeenjääneet paperit on saanut haltuunsa kustannustoimittaja Keserű (Janne Reinikainen), joka haluaisi julkaista ne. Edesmenneen kirjailijan jäämistöstä näyttää kuitenkin puuttuvan olennainen palanen, romaani, jonka olemassaolosta on vain epämääräisiä vihjeitä. Keserű lähtee jäljittämään mestariteosta, joka tuntuu haihtuneen olemattomiin. Kadonneen romaanin etsinnästä kehkeytyy Keserűlle pakkomielle, vuosia kestävä salapoliisimysteeri, johon sekoittuu yhä enemmän ihmisiä: ystäviä, läheisiä, kustannusväkeä, viranomaisia. Kaikkien kohtaloiden ja tarinoiden keskiössä on samaan aikaan läsnä- ja poissaoleva kirjailija B, jonka elämä ja kuolema kietoutuvat Euroopan viime vuosisadan katastrofeihin. summary.en: The Peacock in the Garden – Mathias Withoos and Rome

ai.en: Paintings by Mathias Withoos and other members of the Bentvueghels, the Dutch and Flemish artists' group in Rome. The show runs at the Sinebrychoff Art Museum until January 2027.

events.description: The Peacock in the Garden – Mathias Withoos and Rome Like many of his colleagues, the painter Mathias Withoos joined the Bentvueghels during his stay in Rome around 1648–1653. Rome can be seen in his art in the landscapes, which he framed with abundant plant motifs. In his signature still-life paintings, undergrowth teeming with life is combined with elements from a sublime urban landscape. In his oeuvre he repeatedly returned to Roman and Italian influences. The Bentvueghels group sprang up among Dutch and Flemish artists in Rome around 1620, and the community continued in existence for a century, until 1720. They were boisterous revellers who spent time in close-knit togetherness in their new city. But being in Rome was about more than just carousing. They took art making and artistic development seriously. The members of the Bentvueghels were especially keen on drawing and painting in the open air. The artists wanted to learn from the Italian masters, and also sought out new views in the city. The group included, among others, Caspar van Wittel (1653–1736), Jan Both (1618–1652) and Cornelis van Poelenburgh (1594–1667), whose works are in this exhibition. Sinebrychoff Art Museum, 1st floor 24.9.2026-10.1.2027 Tue, Thu, Fri 11.00-18.00 Wed 10.00-20.00 Sat-Sun 10.00-17.00 Admission fee 0-21€

title.en: Zsuzsa Hullan: The Whole World Is a Stage

summary.en: The photo series The Whole World Is a Stage (Színház az egész…) focuses on theatre and aims to offer a glimpse behind the scenes.

ai.en: A photo series by actress and photographer Zsuzsa Hullan, showing the behind-the-scenes life of theatre, at the Liszt Institute from 25 September to 6 November. Entry is free.

events.description: The photo series The Whole World Is a Stage (Színház az egész…) focuses on theatre and aims to lift the curtain on what happens behind the scenes, offering the general public a glimpse into the lesser-known side of the theatre world. The exhibition is curated by Vera Várszegi. “I am an actress. During performances and rehearsals, I see different situations, scenes and my colleagues from a perspective that is inaccessible to ordinary theatre-goers. When I fell in love with photography, I decided to bring these moments to light.” Zsuzsa Hullan is an actress at Budapest’s renowned Vígszínház theatre and a photographic artist. Her first solo exhibition was held in Budapest in 2019. Since then, her photographs have been featured in numerous exhibitions, including international ones, as well as in publications such as Premier magazine and National Geographic, following a recommendation from Kossuth Prize-winning photographer Éva Keleti. Hullan has also participated in several prestigious photography competitions, receiving numerous awards. Liszt Institute, Galleria U 25.9.-6.11.2026 Instead of an opening reception, there will be an artist talk and guided tour of the exhibition on 28.10 at 18.00: Registration form Mon-Fri 10.00-18.00 Free entry

title.en: Antti Tolvi: For Organ and Pause

summary.en: Antti Tolvi´s work consists of sound, light and beds that vibrate at a low frequency, and it invites you to pause and reflect.

ai.en: "For Organ and Pause" by Antti Tolvi, a long-running sound installation and performance with an organ and beds, open at HAM until January 2027.

events.description: Please come in, lie down and relax. For Organ and Pause is both an installation and a long-duration performance that begins when the exhibition opens and ends when it closes. Together, the sound, light and beds create a slowly evolving and transforming work of art. The continuous sound is produced by the angelica archangelica organ and beds that go quiet six times during the exhibition. These pauses provide space for the performances composed by Tolvi and performed by him together with other musicians. Tolvi is a sound artist and performer with a background in experimental music. Tolvi is fascinated by long-duration performances that challenge our perception of time. A work that goes on for more than three months is impossible to experience from start to finish. Instead, you can quieten down and pause to savour it for a specific, unique moment. Space for New Art is HAM’s new platform for versatile art-making and innovative exhibition concepts. The space offers – engaging both body and mind – captivating encounters with art and artists. The first open call focused on exhibition proposals that enliven the art experience through performative and audience-engaging methods. summary.en: Vaikenemisen kielioppi on visuaalinen näyttämöteos Venäjän sukupuoli- ja seksuaalivähemmistöihin kuuluvien ihmisten kokemuksista 2010-luvulta tähän päivään.

ai.en: "Vaikenemisen kielioppi", a visual theatre piece about LGBTQ+ people's lives in Russia, staged at Vuosaari Tilajakamo from 29 September to 4 November. It is for ages 16 and up.

events.description: Vaikenemisen kielioppi on visuaalinen näyttämöteos Venäjän sukupuoli- ja seksuaalivähemmistöihin kuuluvien ihmisten kokemuksista 2010-luvulta tähän päivään. Se perustuu keskusteluihin Venäjällä elävien ja maasta lähteneiden sateenkaari-ihmisten kanssa – ihmisten, joiden elämässä identiteetti, läheisyys ja näkyväksi tuleminen ovat vähitellen muuttuneet yhä vaarallisemmiksi. 2010-luvulta lähtien LGBTQ+-identiteettien systemaattinen tukahduttaminen Venäjällä on johtanut tilanteeseen, jossa pelkkä olemassaolo voi olla rikos: julkinen ilmaisu, yhteisöt ja symbolit on kriminalisoitu, ja seurauksena ovat pidätykset, maanpako ja hiljaisuus. Mutta mitä hiljaisuudessa tapahtuu? Mitä jää sanomatta ystäville, perheelle, työpaikalla – ja itselle. Esityksen tekijät tutkivat hiljaisuutta ja sitä, mitä hiljaisuudessa tapahtuu. Teoksessa ei ole perinteistä juonta eikä näyttämöllä kerrota haastatteluja sellaisinaan. Haastattelujen tunnelmat, muistot ja sisäiset ristiriidat muuttuvat visuaaliseksi kollaasiksi: esineiksi, materiaaleiksi, nukeiksi, varjoiksi ja näyttelijöiden fyysiseksi ilmaisuksi. Sanat väistyvät, mutta tunteet tulevat näkyviksi. Teoksen ohjaa Venäjältä vuonna 2022 Saksaan lähtenyt venäläinen ohjaaja Roman Boklanov. summary.en: Helios is a seven-metre-scale model of the Sun created by artist Luke Jerram, combining art, light and sound into a captivating artistic experience.

ai.en: "Helios", a seven-metre model of the Sun by Luke Jerram, at Helsinki Cathedral in October. It combines solar imagery with a specially made sound piece. Admission is 8 euros.

events.description: Helios is a seven-metre-scale model of the Sun created by British artist Luke Jerram, combining art, light and sound into a captivating artistic experience. Measuring seven metres in diameter, the artwork features 72dpi detailed imagery* of the Sun’s surface. At an approximate scale of 1:200 million, each centimetre of the internally lit spherical sculpture represents 2000km of the Sun’s surface. The installation is a fusion of solar imagery, sunlight and a specially created sound composition by Duncan Speakman and Sarah Anderson. Imagery for the artwork has been compiled using 400,000 photographs of the Sun provided by Astrophotographer Dr Stuart Green (taken between May 2018 to June 2024) and NASA observations of the Sun, with guidance from solar scientist, Professor Lucie Green of University College London (UCL). Helios follows on from Jerram’s previous astronomical artworks, Museum of the Moon, Gaia, and Mars. In Helsinki, Helios forms part of the Helsinki Cathedral Parish’s Let There Be Light! themed month, which explores mental wellbeing and mental health. Cathedral 1.10.-1.11.2026 The latest opening hours are available on Helsinki Cathedral’s website Admission fee 8€, under 18 yrs free entry

summary.en: A Family Space Adventure - a fun-filled family adventure featuring art, space-themed questions and activities!

ai.en: A family space adventure through October around Luke Jerram's Helios, with art, space questions and activities. It has a short route at the Cathedral and a longer one to the Old Church.

events.description: Join us this October for a fun-filled family adventure featuring art, space-themed questions and activities! Throughout October, families can explore Helios, the spectacular artwork by British artist Luke Jerram, through a series of engaging activities. Helios is a highly detailed scale model of the Sun, presented at approximately 1:200 million scale. The artwork measures seven metres in diameter, with each centimetre representing 2,000 kilometres of the Sun's surface. Thanks to Helios, visitors can examine the surface of our nearest star up close. The imagery is based on 400,000 photographs of the Sun and incorporates observations collected by NASA. During this family-friendly space adventure, you will have the chance to marvel at the giant Sun, answer space-themed questions, and take part in creative activities inspired by space exploration. The adventure can be completed in two ways: a shorter version at Helsinki Cathedral only, or a longer route that takes explorers from Helsinki Cathedral to the Old Church. The Space Adventure is available throughout October, and you may complete it at any time that suits you. title.en: Art exhibition: Valeria Azovskaya - Blooming under pressure

summary.en: Photography has long been my safe ground, a familiar lens for observing, capturing, and making sense of the world.

events.description: Kukoistus paineen alla Tämä näyttely on suodattamaton käännekohta matkallani visuaalisena taiteilijana. Astun pois tutulta alueelta tutkimaan maalausta ja kädentaitoja. Käytän valokuvallista työskentelyäni en lopullisena päämääränä, vaan lähtökohtana. Siirtyminen uuteen välineeseen tuo mukanaan painetta, epävarmuutta eikä mitään takeita. Kasvu edellyttää, että oppii olemaan tässä arvaamattomassa tilassa — ensin sen hyväksyen ja myöhemmin, toivottavasti, itsevarmuudella. Tällä seinällä olevat teokset heijastavat juuri tätä prosessia. Pakottaakseni itseni pois mukavuusalueeltani asetin itselleni tiukan tehtävänannon ja määräajan. Käytän tämän näyttelyn luomaa painetta uusien teosten tekemiseen suoraan valokuvallisista lähtökohdistani. Ilman tätä itse asetettua pakkoa olisi liian helppoa pysyä siellä, missä on turvallista. Sekä valmiina että vielä muotoutuvina nämä teokset edustavat elävää kokeilua — tilaa, jossa valokuva muuttuu maaliksi ja jossa sekä kävijä että minä kohtaamme odottamattoman yhdessä. Tämä kokonaisuus koostuu kahdesta toisiaan täydentävästä teoksesta: Helsinki City Bloom on valokuvapaneeli, joka tallentaa kevätkukkia eri puolilta kaupunkia päivittäisten kävelyjeni aikana, ja Sakura Bloom on kokeellinen maalaus, joka on syntynyt tiukkojen aikarajojen alla ja vie työskentelyä kameran ulkopuolelle tavoittaakseen itse luomisen raa’an, fyysisen liikkeen. Taiteilijasta Valeria Azovskaya on Helsingissä asuva ja työskentelevä suunnittelija ja visuaalinen taiteilija…

summary.en: These artworks created by pupils of Maunula Primary School depict familiar local surroundings

events.description: The neighbourhoods are depicted as green, rugged and inviting, full of meaningful nooks and crannies and places that evoke warm memories. The pupils have drawn inspiration from personal everyday moments: from the home yard, parks, school commutes, and shopping trips. With a special sense of warmth and a through a lens of nostalgia, many pupils have wanted to take a look at the old school building, from which they have moved to temporary premises for the duration of a renovation project. The exhibition offers a glimpse, through 44 works of art, into children’s diverse, endearing and at times even surprising ways of seeing their immediate surroundings. At the same time, it serves as a reminder of how important it is to give children’s art space to be seen. A child’s perspective is important, and every moment counts. Place: Lobby gallery

title.en: Alisa Javits: On Fear and Evil

summary.en: Media Box presents Alisa Javits' On Fear and Evil, a 25-minute short film exploring fear, evil and the relationship between the two.

ai.en: "On Fear and Evil", a 25-minute short film by Alisa Javits that combines anonymous interviews about fear and violence. It is shown at Forum Box from 2 to 25 October. Entry is free.

events.description: Alisa Javits’ On Fear and Evil is a 25-minute short film exploring fear, evil and the relationship between the two. Through personal experiences, the film considers how fear can influence human actions and shape our understanding of good and evil. The film begins with a short reflective prologue and concludes with an epilogue. Between them, a series of anonymous interviews brings forward personal experiences of fear and evil – of the evil the interviewees have done themselves, as well as the evil they have experienced at the hands of others. Remaining anonymous, the interviewees speak from deeply personal experiences while raising questions that extend beyond the individual. Where is the boundary between fear and evil? Alongside the inner world of the human being, nature becomes another presence in the work. Its scale is different: nature exists independently of humanity, even as human beings remain dependent on it in many ways. Within this scale, the violence and evil of human history can appear small. On an individual level, however, evil can be immense. Alisa Javits is a visual artist and creative director whose works explore the experiences of human existence in this world. Alisa’s works are characterized by profound content and versatility. A recurring theme in her work is the contradiction between the inner and outer in people. Forum Box, Mediabox 2.-25.10.2026 Tue-Sun 12.00-17.00 Free entry

summary.en: Going Nowhere brings together works connected by thoughts of division, the distance forming between people, and the growing fragility of shared space.

ai.en: "Going Nowhere", a show of steel and aluminium sculptures by Eetu Huhtala, some of them mechanical, that explore division and distance. It is at Forum Box from 2 to 25 October.

events.description: Split in two, lopsided, and always returning to the starting point. The exhibition Going Nowhere brings together works connected by thoughts of division, the distance forming between people, and the growing fragility of shared space. The exhibition consists of works made of steel and aluminium that borrow their forms and functions from large-scale objects and devices found in public spaces. Individual works are rooted in experiences of supporting structures disappearing, unevenness, and aimlessness. Throughout the works, however, there is a recurring sense of distance and of the impossibility of closing it. Eetu Huhtala (b. 1993, Äänekoski) is a sculptor living in Helsinki and working in Kerava. Huhtala’s practice consists of moving mechanical sculptures, large-scale metal sculptures, and multisensory works. His works are often based on familiar everyday objects, devices, or structures, which, through changes in their function or form, become connected to personal experiences and broader societal problems. Mechanical objects often become flawed in a distinctly human way. Forum Box 2.-25.10.2026 Tue-Sun 12.00-17.00 Free entry

summary.en: Viivi Prokofjev transforms gallery into a space where historical styles converge, and spends a month chopping vegetables as part of an ongoing performance.

ai.en: Viivi Prokofjev's "Chop Chop", the Graphic Designer of the Year 2026 exhibition at Luonnos Gallery. Its performance of chopping vegetables runs for a month, with the opening on 2 October.

events.description: Known as an art director, illustrator and book designer, Viivi Prokofjev transforms Luonnos Gallery into a space where historical styles converge, and spends a month chopping vegetables as part of an ongoing performance. Welcome to the opening of the exhibition on Friday 2 October, 17.00-19.00, at Grafia’s Luonnos Gallery. “Chop chop” means to hurry or rush, yet the exhibition is an exercise in the opposite. Inspired by French culinary traditions, Chop Chop plays with a basic geometric form and explores the relationship between the decorative and the practical. The exhibition brings the often invisible labour of preparation into focus. In addition to the performance, the exhibition consists of spatial design and a Tropism print publication, featuring texts by Benjamin Mouly, Maya Byskov and Sara Karppinen on the relationship between form and matter, as well as kitchen practices and rituals. title.en: Igor Lora Romero: Developing Bodies in Space (2021)

summary.en:
Projection of the short animation Developing Bodies in Space (2021) by Igor Lora Romero
5th to 30th October 2026
Projection walls on the 1st floor of Oodi

ai.en: A projection of Igor Lora Romero's animation "Developing Bodies in Space" on the first-floor walls of Oodi, from 5 to 30 October. It explores the link between body and mind.

events.description: Projection of the short animation Developing Bodies in Space (2021) by Igor Lora Romero Projection walls on the 1st floor of Oodi 5th to 30th October 2026 The film explores the relationships between body and mind, creator and creation. How can an individual create physical proof that their conscience existed in this very moment? A piece of paper is pressed against the skin so that its creases become a map, but something is lost in translation. Just as tridimensionality is incomprehensible for a surface, we are only able to understand our surroundings through our senses. What lies outside of our perception? How does it feel to be something (or someone) else outside of our body? The artist is a student of the Master in Fine Arts in the University of the Arts Helsinki. Inspired by introspection and concerns from everyday life, his pieces cover a range of topics such as personal identity,the human body or the search of beauty. Most recently he has been working with figurative paintings andhandmade models. Instagram: @tanelfu Developing Bodies is part of Oodi Media Art Exhibitions series 2026-2027: Media Art Open Call 2026-2027 - Oodi

summary.en: In her oil paintings, Emma Ainala opens up a seductive and chaotic world before the museum visitor.

ai.en: "Like a Prayer", an exhibition of Emma Ainala's paintings from the past ten years, mostly of women and girls in nature or enclosed rooms, with references to pop culture and art history. It is at Kiasma.

events.description: The main characters in Emma Ainala's works are often girls and women who linger amid luxuriant nature or in enclosed interiors. Some have transformed into spiders or snakes. One bears the features of a sphinx, while others have taken on the form of a centaur. The exhibition presents Ainala’s works from the past ten years, bringing together both new paintings and key works from across her career. According to the artist, the exhibition title Like a Prayer refers both to the act of painting and to viewing artworks. In both situations, an individual is faced with something unknown. It is a moment that calls for letting go of control and trusting intuition. Ainala’s richly detailed paintings are filled with references to popular culture, fashion and art history. Through her art, she seeks to defend the multifacetedness of life: alongside limiting roles, there can also be joy and possibility. In her works, women are compared to pet animals and blend into the décor around them, yet they also glow brightly in the darkness.

title.en: Emma Talbot: You Are Not the Centre

summary.en: British artist Emma Talbot fills HAM’s grand arched hall with glowing colours, flowing patterns, and poetic handwritten texts.

ai.en: "You Are Not the Centre", a show by Emma Talbot at HAM with silk paintings, textiles and drawings, and an animation that puts humans back among other living things. It runs until April 2027.

events.description: In her art, Emma Talbot (b. 1969) explores relationships between humans and nature in an era defined by the climate crisis, biodiversity loss and technological change. The artist’s own experiences and reflections expand from the personal towards the collective, forming narratives of the present day. For Talbot, drawing forms the foundation of her artistic practice, serving both as a tool for thinking and a channel for emotions. The exhibition features large-scale silk paintings, three-dimensional textile works, as well as drawings. Together, they create a spatial installation in which the viewer can move as if following the artist’s train of thought. Talbot’s handwritten texts are an integral part of the works, opening up new perspectives on them. Also on view is the animation You Are Not the Centre, in which the narrator figure experiences the world through the senses of a dog, a spider, a bird, a deer and a moth. The animation challenges anthropocentric worldview by highlighting the intelligence and emotional capacity of the animal kingdom. In Emma Talbot’s works, humans are not placed at the centre of the world, but as part of nature and a larger whole whose pieces are interdependent. The exhibition invites to reflect on how people can collectively envision more sustainable and equitable futures. HAM 9.10.2026-25.4.2027 Tue 10.00–17.00 Wed-Fri 11.00–19.00 Sat-Sun 11.00–17.00 Admission fee 0-20€

summary.en: Resting wild cats, references to various cultures, and personal messages permeate her large-scale, vibrantly coloured pieces.

ai.en: "Misfit", the first joint show of Leena Luostarinen's monumental paintings from the 1980s and 1990s, from HAM's collection. It runs until April 2027.

events.description: Leena Luostarinen (1949–2013) ranks among Finland’s most distinguished painters, who left an indelible mark on the Finnish art world. Now presented together for the first time, the exhibitionbrings together Luostarinen’s monumental paintings from HAM’s collection, dating from what is considered her creative peak in the 1980s and 1990s. Luostarinen made her breakthrough in 1981 with a solo exhibition of large-scale feline predators. She soon became known for powerful paintings that visibly bear the marks of their making – from palette-knife traces to vigorous brushstrokes. In 1988, she was named Finland’s Artist of the Year. Despite the acclaim she received, she often felt like an outsider, sensing that she neither belonged nor could conform. She travelled widely, driven by a longing for distant places. Drawing on influences from many cultures, she developed a compelling, recognisable style that resists categorisation. The exhibition architecture draws its colour scheme from Luostarinen’s paintings, while subtly mimicking the symmetrical floor plan of an imaginary temple. Feline creatures guide the visitors through the exhibition, which is arranged neither chronologically nor thematically. HAM 9.10.2026-4.4.2027 Tue 10.00–17.00 Wed-Fri 11.00–19.00 Sat-Sun 11.00–17.00 Admission fee 0-20€

summary.en: An award-winning immersive journey 3,400 years back to ancient Egypt through 360° projections, VR and an interactive virtual world.

ai.en: "Tutankhamun: The Immersive Exhibition", on its first visit to Finland, with 360-degree projections, a VR journey and replicas of the treasures. It is at Malmi Ice Hall until 24 January 2027, for ages 6 and up.

events.description: Having captivated more than 2.5 million visitors worldwide, Tutankhamun – The Immersive Exhibition arrives in Finland for the first time. The award-winning exhibition takes visitors on a journey 3,400 years back in time to ancient Egypt and into the world of the young Pharaoh Tutankhamun. Visitors can explore the era of Tutankhamun, the culture of ancient Egypt and its famous treasures through historical content and highly detailed replicas produced in Egypt based on the original objects. The exhibition features three distinct digital experiences. In a large immersive space, six-metre-high 360-degree projections, music and storytelling surround visitors with the landscapes and temples of ancient Egypt. A VR experience takes visitors on a journey into the ancient Egyptian afterlife, while an interactive virtual world allows them to walk through the Valley of the Kings in 1922 and experience the story of the discovery of Tutankhamun's tomb. Before arriving in Finland, Tutankhamun – The Immersive Exhibition has toured 20 countries and has also been presented at the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza. The exhibition is officially supported by the Grand Egyptian Museum and its audiovisual production has received three international Telly Awards. Malmi Ice Hall 10.10.2026–24.1.2027 Tickets 16,90/21,90€ from Lippupiste Age recommendation 6+

title.en: A Glimpse of the Sampo Collection

summary.en: The new exhibition opening at Villa Gyllenberg in October 2026 presents a rare opportunity to glimpse the impressive art collection belonging to Sampo Group.

ai.en: A selection of about 50 works from the Sampo Group's art collection, including 19th-century landscapes and Finnish Golden Age paintings, at Villa Gyllenberg until 14 February 2027.

events.description: The new exhibition opening at Villa Gyllenberg presents a rare opportunity to glimpse the impressive art collection belonging to Sampo Group. Approximately 50 works have been selected from Sampo’s collection of over 1000 works to be displayed classically. The exhibition presents 19th-century landscape paintings, works from the Golden Age of Finnish art, 20th-century abstract art, and paintings and sculptures from the 1980s and 1990s. The Sampo insurance company was founded in 1909. The company has purposefully collected art for its business premises and offices, especially in the 1970s–1990s. The collection has acquired numerous classics of Finnish painting, as well as examples of high-quality non-representational art. Villa Gyllenberg 10.10.2026-14.2.2027 Wed, Sat & Sun 12.00-17.00 Admission fee 10/12€, under 18 yrs free entry

title.en: Jyrki Tammi: Listen for a Moment

summary.en: Through his works, Jyrki Tammi brings his own experience of silence to the downstairs exhibition space of Galleria Kookos.

ai.en: Jyrki Tammi's paintings, based on textures from nature such as water, sky and ice, shown in the downstairs space of Galleria Kookos from 13 to 24 October. The space invites quiet and a pause from everyday noise.

events.description: "My works explore nature and the human being through oil, acrylic, and mixed-media painting. I begin my process with forms found in nature. Rather than depicting landscapes in the traditional sense, I start with an abstract texture, usually inspired by an element of nature: flowing water, the sky, earth, snow, or ice. The sounds of nature—the rustling of trees, flowing water, or birdsong—have a calming effect and help us detach from everyday life. In nature, sounds themselves are part of silence. They invite to stop and sense what the planet is whispering. Through my works, I bring my own experience of silence to the downstairs exhibition space of Galleria Kookos. This intimate and peaceful space can encourage visitors to pause, step away from excessive sensory stimulation, and experience art through a sense of presence in the moment." Jyrki Tammi Jyrki Tammi (b. 1978) is a visual artist based in Kuusamo, Finland. He graduated with a Master of Arts degree from the University of Lapland in 2019. Before completing his master's degree, he studied art and cultural fields extensively. In his works, chance and control alternate. The juxtaposition of different visual motifs creates distinctive and fresh symbolism. Galleria Kookos, Studio 13.-24.10.2026 Vernissage 13.10. at 18.00-20.00 Tue-Fri 13.00-18.00 Sat 13.00-17.00 Free entry

title.en: Finnish National Youth Theatre: if you ask us

summary.en: The National Youth Theatre is a group of young theatre makers who challenge the understanding of who is allowed to make theatre and who it is for.

ai.en: "If you ask us", a play by the Finnish National Youth Theatre, a group of young theatre makers from several countries. It runs at the National Theatre's Small Stage from 14 October to 2 November, for ages 12 and up.

events.description: The National Youth Theatre is a group of young theatre makers who challenge the understanding of who is allowed to make theatre and who it is for. The group includes performers from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Finland, Kurdistan, Somalia and Syria, who work together with experienced artists. The script is based on material produced by the young people. "if you ask us is not based on a play or ready-made script. All the material has been created in the rehearsal room through different practices of improvisation and task-based scores. Then, the material has been edited and developed together with the actors. We use processes of theatre making so that we can understand and influence how we are represented. This group began working in January 2026. Together we have been learning to listen – to each other and to the world, listening to words and listening to movement. Our stage finds its frame from questions of language, truth, tradition and modernity. Seeking understanding is a constant process of back-and-forth movement." summary.en: A black cat crosses the road, a mirror breaks, the same number appears over again, and a dream feels too precise to dismiss.

events.description: A black cat crosses the road, a mirror breaks, the same number appears over again, and a dream feels too precise to dismiss. Superstition art exhibition brings together works that explore the deeply human tendency to look for patterns, connections, and explanations, even where none may exist. The artists approach superstition through omens, symbols, rituals, dreams, numbers, animals, objects, and personal associations. Crows, ladders, mirrors, repeated signs and accidental encounters become part of a visual vocabulary shaped by both inherited beliefs and individual experience. summary.en: Antti Jussila’s Tender Buttons is a kind of home. Its order emerges through small shifts, repetition and things that have temporarily found their place.

ai.en: Antti Jussila's small assemblages at Photographic Gallery Hippolyte, which run alongside Gertrude Stein's "Tender Buttons" and Charlotte Perkins Gilman's "The Yellow Wallpaper". It is free, from 16 October to 15 November.

events.description: Antti Jussila’s Tender Buttons is a kind of home. Its order emerges through small shifts, repetition and things that have temporarily found their place. A home is held together through maintenance: surfaces are wiped, objects are moved, food is prepared and its remains cleared away. Something is constantly accumulating again. Running alongside Jussila’s work are Gertrude Stein’s Tender Buttons (1914) and Charlotte Perkins Gilman’s The Yellow Wallpaper (1892), in which everyday objects, food, rooms and their surfaces refuse to remain merely the backdrop to events. In Jussila’s small-scale assemblages, repeated patterns and overlapping window frames are interwoven with plaster, textiles and everyday materials. Vaseline, glitter and food remains have adhered to smooth picture surfaces; elsewhere, small objects and materials are embedded in plaster, while clean textiles come into contact with those that have become soiled. Antti Jussila (b. 1979) is an artist based in Helsinki. He works across sculpture, moving image, sound and performance, both independently and collectively. His work brings visuality, materiality and language together, allowing meanings to accumulate in layers. His practice repeatedly examines systems and the interdependencies between them, alongside speculative fiction, the liminal zones of consciousness and aesthetic dead ends. Photographic Gallery Hippolyte 16.10.-15.11.2026 Free entry

title.en: Wanda & Naomi Holopainen: Landscape of Traces

summary.en: Wanda and Naomi Holopainen’s exhibition explores archives, memory and the ways knowledge is passed between generations and places.

ai.en: "Landscape of Traces" by Wanda and Naomi Holopainen at Photographic Gallery Hippolyte, on archives, memory and what is carried across generations. Entry is free, from 16 October to 15 November.

events.description: Landscape of Traces, an exhibition by artists Wanda Holopainen and Naomi Holopainen, continues their collaborative exploration of archives, memory and the ways in which knowledge is carried across generations and places. The exhibition examines how histories are remembered, preserved and passed on through objects, materials and practices. It considers how our relationship with things from the past shapes what remains, what is left out and what is forgotten. Landscape of Traces invites visitors to consider what remains in the materials around us and the stories they carry. What do we choose to reclaim, preserve, care for and pass on? What might exist beyond what we can see? Wanda Holopainen (b. 1993) is a self-taught multidisciplinary installation artist. Her current practice brings together textile installation, moving image and photography to explore material memory, ecology, transformation and cultural transmission. Naomi Holopainen (b. 1993) works conceptually across different media, exploring lines, forms and movement. Her practice focuses on how materials, bodies and spaces carry traces of experience, and how ordinary materials can be transformed through touch, process and environment. Grounded in collective creation and spatiality, her work explores the relationships between materials, bodies and their surroundings. Photographic Gallery Hippolyte 16.10.-15.11.2026 Free entry

summary.en: Roots en Route is a multi-sensory installation by 4 artists who will create a multi-sensory installation in dialogue with the Kaisaniemi Botanic Garden.

ai.en: "Roots en Route", a multi-sensory installation at Kaisaniemi Botanic Garden about rootedness and displacement, with soundscape, scent and drawings. It runs from 18 October 2026 to 10 January 2027.

events.description: Roots en Route is a multi-sensory installation by four artists who will create a multi-sensory installation in dialogue with this special site, the Kaisaniemi Botanic Garden — examining rootedness and displacement; asking what grows where it was planted and what survives the crossing. The African plants that fill these glasshouses carry their own histories of movement and adaptation. Camille Norment in collaboration with Sofia Jernberg create a soundscape drawing on the birds of the plants' homelands. Toubab Holmes' site-specific scent installation traces the hidden journeys of plants through the extractive system of perfumery. Charmaine Watkiss visits the botanical legacies and healing traditions of her Caribbean ancestry through large-scale drawings of Plant Warriors. Together, the three works read the botanical garden as an archive of movement, and the plants in it as things that were carried, taken and made to travel. events.description: Kirjaston monitoimitilassa on esillä Shaista Malikin käsintehtyjä tekstiili- ja pintakuviotöitä. Shaista Malik on itseoppinut taiteilija ja muotoilija Pakistanista. A first Finnish exhibition of original, hand-made textile and surface designs by Shaista Malik, a self-taught artist and designer from Pakistan. The works were made by hand and brought to Helsinki by the artist: painted pattern and repeat designs, monochrome studies, tie-dyed and block-printed fabrics, smocking, hand and ribbon embroidery, fashion illustration and pencil pattern drawings. The work draws on Pakistani craft traditions, nature and colour. For a Finnish audience, it offers a close look at hand-made surface design from another textile culture, shown as the original cloth and paper rather than as reproductions. summary.en: Discover Life in Colour, Bresley Mansio’s solo exhibition celebrating vibrant colours, Mexican roots, and Día de los Muertos traditions.

ai.en: "Life in Colour" by Bresley Mansio at Mimosa Galleria from 22 October to 3 November. The paintings explore colour and memory, and include a Día de los Muertos altar. Entry is free.

events.description: Life in Colour is an exploration of colour, light, emotion, memory, and belonging. Through vibrant hues and expressive imagery, Bresley Mansio invites visitors to experience colour not only as a visual element, but as a language through which feelings, memories, and cultural roots can find expression. The exhibition also invites visitors to discover the tradition of Día de los Muertos, the Mexican Day of the Dead. This meaningful celebration honours loved ones who have passed away while keeping their memory present through flowers, photographs, candles, favourite objects, and offerings arranged on an altar known as an ofrenda. The altar creates a space for remembrance, connection, and reflection. Its colours and objects carry personal stories, symbolising the continuing bonds between the living and those who are remembered. Life in Colour does not seek to define identity or offer a single answer to the question of belonging. Instead, it opens a space for reflection and personal interpretation. The paintings and the altar invite visitors to consider their own relationships with colour, culture, memory, and emotion. A particular shade may recall a place, a person, a childhood memory, or a feeling that has remained unnamed. Each visitor may discover something different, shaped by their own experiences and connections. Mimosa Galleria 22.10.-3.11.2026 Vapaa pääsy

title.en: COMING SOON: PUNK! 50 years of buzz in the streets of Helsinki

summary.en: Leather jackets and mohawks, zines and self-published albums, sweaty gigs and a DIY attitude. The ex…

ai.en: The "PUNK, 50 years of buzz in the streets of Helsinki" exhibition at Villa Hakasalmi, tracing Finnish punk from late-1970s venues to today with photographs, zines, album covers and a practice space.

events.description:
Leather jackets and mohawks, zines and self-published albums, sweaty gigs and a DIY attitude. The exhibition ‘PUNK! 50 years of buzz in the streets of Helsinki’ takes visitors to key meeting spaces from the late 1970s to the present day – from the Kill City neighbourhood to the Lepakko urban culture centre, and from the legendary second-hand record shop Oskun Divari to the Vuoritalo centre for alternative culture. You can watch the story of Finnish punk unfold through photographs, video interviews, album covers, zines, gig posters, clothing, musical instruments and other artefacts, such as a drum stool built by Pelle Miljoona himself and Maukka Perusjätkä ’s chainsaw.

Punk breaks out of the displays

Punk classics are playing on the jukebox, and you can pogo in the pit or pick up an instrument in the practice space. Through the young band Mökä , visitors get to see how punk music is made in the 2020s. The exhibition also sheds light on punk’s journey from an oppressed subculture to being part of Finnish cultural history. Punk emerged in London and New York in the mid-1970s, giving a voice to the rebellious youth. Despite opposition from the Finnish Government and youth organisations, this counter-culture also drew in Helsinki residents who had grown tired of elitist rock music. Half a century later, punk is still alive and well, living on in art, fashion and activism.

The past calls, the present answers

The exhibition has been curated by Teijo Hintikka…

title.en: Marja Patrikainen & Tuukka Peltonen: Strange Dale

summary.en: The joint exhibition by Marja Patrikainen and Tuukka Peltonen brings together mixed-media sculptures and woodcuts.

ai.en: "Strange Dale", mixed-media sculptures by Marja Patrikainen and woodcuts by Tuukka Peltonen at HAA Gallery from 23 October to 15 November. Entry is free, and the gallery is also open on Viapori Kekri on 31 October.

events.description: The exhibition brings together mixed-media sculptures and woodcuts. Marja Patrikainen’s sculptures explore an alternative experience of nature. Assembled from recycled materials, her animal figures seem like dreamlike visions from another reality, while hinting at the consequences of overconsumption. In Tuukka Peltonen’s woodcuts, human figures inhabit striking natural landscapes. Marja Patrikainen draws inspiration from dreams, the mythologies of different cultures, and pop culture. Her work is shaped by the aesthetics and material choices associated with Indigenous cultures and ITE art (Finnish contemporary folk art). She primarily uses materials that have been gifted, found, salvaged, or bought at flea markets. Her sculptures act as messengers from an imagined reality, addressing concerns about contemporary life. Tuukka Peltonen works in woodcut, with the possibilities of the “vanishing block” technique playing a particularly important role in his practice. He began making woodcuts more than 25 years ago while studying at Kankaanpää Art School. The human figure has been central to Peltonen’s work from the outset. It becomes a symbol in relation to the surrounding environment, as the figures’ inner worlds bring the past into the present. His imagery makes room for dreamers and outsiders alike. HAA Gallery 23.10.-15.11.2026 Free entry Open also on Viapori Kekri, Saturday, October 31, 12.00-18.00

summary.en: The journey is more important than the destination.  Nanna Susi's painting cycles span different eras and journeys through life.

ai.en: "piano piano", a painting exhibition by Nanna Susi at her studio from 23 October to 15 November, inspired partly by a trip to Japan. Entry is free.

events.description: The journey is more important than the destination. My painting cycles span different eras and journeys through life. In creating these latest paintings, I have reflected especially on the importance of the journey – and on the simple act of being present in the moment. Piano piano means “slowly, slowly”: slowing down and embracing stillness. Piano piano is like a peacefully turning perpetual-motion machine, unfolding one moment after another. For me, the guiding idea behind piano piano and the paintings in this exhibition has been to savour life, to enjoy simply being, and to engage in a kind of tranquil stretching of both thought and feeling. As I have painted, piano piano has become a new landscape for me, one in which I have found myself dreaming new dreams. The paintings are partly inspired by my travels in Japan in early 2026. In my painting process, piano piano has come to signify a journey between what is seen and what is still emerging. It has been a welcome and peaceful respite from life’s endless marathon, and it will remain a dear friend for the rest of my life. Most of the paintings in this exhibition feature sunrises, sunsets, and clouds that seem to take the shape of thoughts. In all their simplicity." Helsinki, October 1, 2026 nanna susi studio 23.10.-15.11.2026 Mon-Fri 12.00–18.00 Sat-Sun 11.00–16.00 Free entry

summary.en: Ken Matsubara: Moon, no thought of reflection. Water, no thought of reflecting.

ai.en: "Moon, no thought of reflection. Water, no thought of reflecting.", Ken Matsubara's first solo show in Finland, with a new site-specific video installation at Helsinki Contemporary. It runs from 2 to 25 October, and entry is free.

events.description: Ken Matsubara (b. 1949 in Tokyo) is a Japanese artist who primarily works with video art. Moon, no thought of reflection. Water, no thought of reflecting. is Matsubara’s first solo exhibition in Finland. At Helsinki Contemporary, visitors will be able to experience a new site-specific video installation by the artist, as well as works combining objects and moving image. Ken Matsubara’s work addresses memories and histories to which all canrelate, regardless of backgrounds. Matsubara is interested in how memory can extend beyond individual experience, resonating across generations and different cultures. His understated and meditative works reflect on time and the transience of being, as well as the invisible forces and collective memory invested in objects. Ken Matsubara has held solo exhibitions and participated in museum shows in Japan and internationally since the 1980s. His works are in major collections in Europe, USA, and Asia. His works are currently on view also in EMMA Espoo Museum of Modern Art’s exhibition In Search of the Present: On Rootlessness, on view until February 2027. Helsinki Contemporary 2.-25.10.2026 Wed-Fri 12.00-18.00 Sat-Sun 12.00-16.00 Free entry

summary.en: Tiina Ketaras solo exhibition "Ilmaan ripustetut hetket" at Galleria Pirkko-Liisa Topelius.

ai.en: Tiina Ketara's bead sculptures at Pirkko-Liisa Topelius gallery, from 20 October to 8 November. They include a life-size work inspired by Steinbeck's The Red Pony, and a jumper leaping into the unknown.

events.description: "My exhibiton consists of six bead sculptures from the past few years. As my main mediums, I work with bead sculptures and installations. This year I have completed a largescale sculpture Punainen poni. The sculpture is lifesize and inspired by the novella The Red Pony by John Steinbeck. The work deals with dreams, hope, responsibility, letting go and death. The two largescale works on display are Hyppy tuntemattomaan and Pommihyppy. In Hyppy tuntemattomaan a jumper leaps into the unknown full of joy and anticipation. Through this life carries the jumper, that depicts the moment before a crash into water. Other works include Kädenojennus. It depicts a hand lifting another into the air, as if from water or a deep pit. The work deals with themes of support and supporting. Kyynel depicts a large teardrop falling from the ceiling. Riivahenki deals with physical and mental possession. Beads make up the whole of the sculpture ”body”. Beads are suspended from a line attached to a polycarbonate structure suspended from the ceiling with hooks and wires. This gives the illusion of the sculpture floating. These works are like momentary flashes. In my works I aim to utilise the qualities of beads with whom I aim to crystallise archetypal shapes and memories. I aim to create a spellbinding atmosphere or feeling." Tiina Ketara Galleria Pirkko-Liisa Topelius 20.10.-8.11.2026 Free entry

summary.en:
Artists Heidi Heinonen and Maj Sjö’s joint exhibition, Between Earth and Sky, brings together two distinct forms of visual expression.
28 September – 24 October

ai.en: "Between Earth and Sky", paintings by Heidi Heinonen and Maj Sjö on nature, memory and colour, at Galleria Dromig.

events.description: Between Earth and Sky brings together two distinct forms of visual expression. One opens up the landscape, while the other fills it with life. Together, they invite the viewer to enter a natural world where openness and abundance complement one another. The paintings of Heidi Heinonen and Maj Sjö approach nature from different perspectives, yet share a common foundation. Both artists work intuitively, building their paintings through layers and placing a strong trust in colour – in its subtle nuances as well as its powerful contrasts. Maj Sjö’s works unfold as spaces in which colour, light and form are experienced as moods rather than recognisable landscapes. Heidi Heinonen, in turn, creates lush botanical worlds inspired by a longing for nature’s abundance and richness of colour. The paintings do not depict a particular season as observed, but rather an experience of nature shaped by memory, anticipation and imagination. Although the artists’ visual languages are distinct, their works are united by the constant presence of nature, an intuitive approach to painting and a desire to interpret the world around them. The exhibition invites us to pause and experience nature – not through predetermined answers, but through our own observations and experiences. Heidi Heinonen Heidi Heinonen works with acrylic paint. Her works often develop through a lengthy process in which colours, forms and layers gradually find their own order. Music is an important starting point for her…

summary.en: Lizzy’s paintings transform inherited symbols across cultural boundaries, creating contemplative spaces. Welcome to the opening.

ai.en: "The Presence of Vajra" by Lizzy HyoLa Kim at Take Me Home Gallery from 7 to 31 October, blending Korean Buddhist symbols with Baroque and Rococo ornament. Entry is free.

events.description: Jeju Island based artist Lizzy HyoLa Kim develops a contemporary visual language at the intersection of Korean Buddhist heritage and Western art history. Raised within a three-generation Buddhist temple family at Sanbangsan Bomunsa, founded by her grandfather and subsequently led by her father and younger brother, she approaches Buddhism not as inherited iconography alone, but as a living cultural and philosophical foundation for her practice. Leaving Jeju at thirteen, she continued her education in California and later studied art in New York. Her experiences across the US, Korea, and European museums and art scenes shaped a practice in which Eastern symbolism enters into dialogue with the visual languages of Baroque and Rococo ornamentation. At its center is the Vajra, the Buddhist symbol of indestructibility, clarity, and wisdom. Reconstructed through ribbons, symmetry, decorative structures, and Western ornamental forms, the Vajra becomes both sacred object and contemporary metaphor: a recurring meditation on resilience, balance, and inner clarity. Take Me Home-Gallery 7.-31.10.2026 Free entry

title.en: W. A. Mozart: Requiem – Utopia 25 Years

summary.en: Mozart’s Requiem performed by world-class musicians. Featuring Kamarikuoro Utopia, soloists, and instrumental ensemble.

ai.en: A Finnish premiere of an arrangement of Mozart's Requiem for small ensemble, performed by Utopia Chamber Choir and soloists at the German Church on 24 October. Tickets cost 30 to 35 euros.

events.description: In Mozart’s Requiem, anger meets consolation and fear finds peace. More than 200 years after the composer’s death, it remains a work that invites reflection and stillness. In the early nineteenth century, a rare arrangement of the Requiem was created for the cathedral of Évora in Portugal, scored for a small ensemble of soloists, choir, organ, and instrumentalists. This version will now be heard in Finland for the first time. The intimate ensemble brings this familiar masterpiece closer to the listener. Beneath the arches of the German Church, the Requiem is not a distant monument. Every voice and every word emerges with clarity, revealing colours and details that can be lost within the sound of a large orchestra. The Requiem will be performed by Utopia Chamber Choir together with a distinguished group of musicians. The soloists are Titta Lampela, soprano, Iris Oja, alto, Charles Barbier, tenor, and Jussi Lehtipuu, bass. At the organ is early music specialist Andrew Lawrence-King. The ensemble also features bassoonists Otto Virtanen and Jaakko Luoma, cellist Heidi Peltoniemi, and double bassist Eero Marttila. Utopia’s 25th anniversary concert. One evening. Finnish premiere. German Church 24.10.2026 17.00-18.00 Tickets 35/30€ from Holvi Shop

events.description: Shared Frequencies: Pixelache Festival 2026 (K18) Tänä vuonna Pixelache-festivaali järjestetään Suvilahdessa 20.–24. Lokakuuta. Arkipäivisin järjestetään työpajoja Oranssilla ja lauantaina Tiivistämöllä on tarjolla elokuvanäytöksiä, esityksiä ja musiikkia. Elämme epävarmaa aikaa, jossa julkinen keskustelu tuntuu yhä enemmän rakentuvan sodan, kriisien ja katastrofien ympärille. Selviytymistä käsitellään helposti yksilön omana projektina: jokaisen pitäisi varautua itse, hankkia selviytymispakkaus ja pitää huolta vain omasta pärjäämisestään. Tälläisessa tilanteessa taiteella voi olla toinen tehtävä. Sen sijaan, että keskitymme yksilölliseen selviytymiseen, taide voi auttaa meitä rakentamaan yhteisiä tapoja toimia, ajatella ja kuvitella tulevaisuutta. Emme ehkä itse koskaan näe sellaista maailmaa, jonka haluaisimme, mutta voimme silti pitää yllä toivoa ja välittää sitä eteenpäin seuraaville sukupolville. Pixelache-festivaalin tämän vuoden teema käsittelee solidaarisuutta ja yhteistyötä vaihtoehtona ajatukselle, että vain vahvimmat selviävät. Festivaali etsii hitaita ja yhteisöllisiä tapoja rakentaa verkostoja, joissa ihmiset voivat tukea toisiaan ja luoda yhdessä jotain uutta. Lopulta teema on kuitenkin vain tapa kehystää festivaalia. Tärkeintä on tehdä asioita yhdessä, kokeilla uusia tapoja olla ja toimia yhdessä, pitäen samalla myös hauskaa. Festivaaliaikataulu Tiivistämöllä la 24.10: Red Dawns: Valikoima lyhytvideoita Slovenialaiselta feministisen ja queer-taiteen…

events.description: Swan Lake comes to Finlandia Hall for two performances in October 2026! British Festival Ballet presents the classical ballet in Helsinki, with guest artists Yerkin Rakhmatullayev and Sofiya Adilkhanova from Astana Opera in the leading roles. A prince, a swan and a spell. By day, Odette is transformed into a swan on an enchanted lake. By night, she returns to human form. Prince Siegfried falls in love with her and promises to break the curse, until the sorcerer Rothbart sends his daughter Odile disguised in Odette’s image. The dual role of Odette and Odile is one of the defining roles of the classical ballet repertoire, contrasting the lyrical White Swan with the virtuosity of the Black Swan. The production follows the classical tradition associated with the 1895 staging of Swan Lake, with choreography based on Marius Petipa and Lev Ivanov and music by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky. The performances feature a full corps de ballet under the artistic direction of Yassaui and Sophie Mergaliyev. title.en: Entanglement: I am a tree, I am a mouth

summary.en: The multidisciplinary performance combines video technology with live performing, transforming the Kiasma Theatre stage into an ancient oak forest.

ai.en: "Entanglement: I am a tree, I am a mouth", a sensory performance at Kiasma Theatre that mourns the loss of our connection with ancient oaks. It runs on 24, 25, 28 and 30 October, and the ticket includes Kiasma's exhibitions.

events.description: The performance is a sensory elegy that mourns our loss of connection to arboreal kin. Interweaving movement, sound and images, the work invites the audience into the entangled connections between an ancient oak grove, the human body and more-than-human beings — a ritual in the presence of a vanishing nature. This interdisciplinary performance installation emerges from the Entanglement collective’s field research in the ancient oak grove of Vaarniemi, Kaarina — a Natura 2000 site explored through listening and sensory attention since 2022. The collective’s artistic exploration generates an unfolding aesthetic-embodied ecosystem, stimulating the senses and emotions, and is intended to prompt contemplation about our role in preserving biodiversity. WORKING GROUP: Maria Nurmela , Vesa Loikas, Jane Sheldon, Jaakko Vastapuu, Erno Seppälä, Gesa Piper, Riina Kalmi , Bart H.M.Vandeput PERFORMANCES Sat 24.10.2026 15.00 Sun 25.10.2026 15.00 Wed 28.10.2026 18.00 Fri 30.10.2026 18.00 Ticket includes admission to Kiasma's exhibions on the day of the performance.
